en.title: Replace Nth Consonant
en.description:
Replace every n-th English consonant in message with the next consonant in alphabetical order; preserve case and leave all other characters unchanged. In the source example output `CodeTignam`, the uppercase T conflicts with the original lowercase s, the case-preservation rule, and the explanation; this site corrects it to `Codetignam` according to the written rules and the explanation.

The ASCII character set, bounds, and standard input/output format below are a contract supplemented by this site and are not claimed to be original constraints of the source problem.
en.input: Two lines of input: the first line is message (1..200000 ASCII characters, without newlines); the second line is an integer n (1≤n≤200000). Only ASCII A-Z/a-z take part in the consonant check; the vowels are a, e, i, o, u, and y is treated as a consonant; all other ASCII characters are kept as is.
en.output: Output the entire transformed message line.
en.explanation: Scan the string while maintaining the number of consonants seen; whenever the count is a multiple of n, advance one step in the cycle formed by the 21 English consonants.
